GCC's inline block-clear (clear_storage) code, not hand-writable C: head alignment with a lone `swl $zero`, a 32-byte unrolled store loop (4 stores, addiu, 4 stores, bne, sw -4), 4-byte loop, byte tail (a plain C byte loop can't yield the single `swl`; C gives swl+swr pairs).
Tried: `memset(...)` (declared and undeclared), `__builtin_memset`, `bzero`, `__builtin_bzero`, plus -fbuiltin via try_compiler -> this KMC gcc always emits `jal ?memset`/`jal ?bzero`. Builtins ARE on in the harness (verified `abs()` inlines to bgez/negu), so KMC 2.7.2 simply has no memset/bzero builtin. search_flags: all 6 variants identical (3850). IDO 5.3/7.1 can't compile the implicit decl.
Best attempt (score 3850): `void func_8007FFE0(void *arg0, s32 arg1) { bzero(arg0, arg1); }` (`memset(arg0,0,arg1)` scored 4090). Bottleneck: needs a spelling of memset/bzero that KMC expands to clear_storage, or the original was built with another compiler; nothing hand-written will produce it.

Matched first try. It is an init function for the board: writes D_80356FC8/CC/D0/D4=0, D_80356960=1, D_80356962=2, D_80356FD8=arg1, D_80356FDD=2, D_80356FDC=0x32 (no Expansion Pak, D_80000300==0) or 0x3C, D_802AF1C1=0; six 8-byte copies via func_800801A0; then func_80081E20(0xFE); func_800821C0(&D_801115F0 + arg0*0x50); func_80082730(1); func_80082160(lbl,D_803569D4,0x29A,arg1); func_80080570 with ids 4/9/0xE and msg 0x29B/0x29C/0x29D; three func_80081480 panels (0x13/0x78, 0x12/0x6E, 0x11/0x64) each followed by func_80081640. Pointers must be passed as arrays (D_xxx[0]) so the args are plain addresses.

Matched as s32 func(s32) (float stream-byte generator). The callers func_8007522C/7C/CC instead declare `u8 func_8007423C(u8);` locally and that is what reproduces the ROM: with the u8 return the caller emits no `andi` mask before storing/adding the result (target has just `addu v1,v0,zero`). Do not put a shared s32 prototype in context.h: it breaks those three matched callers.

Matched first try. main's init: clears the callback pointer D_80325428, func_8006FA20(), func_8006E550(0x10,1), func_80082210(0x5A), then a 6-arg func_80081480(D_8029E160,3,func_8002AAF4,NULL,D_80303AB0,0xA) + func_80081640(D_8029E160) and func_80081570(D_8029DFB0,0), then `while (1) { if (D_80325428 != NULL) D_80325428(); }`. NOTE the -O0 infinite-loop idiom: the loop head is `j body; nop; j exit; nop` (the second, dead jump to the epilogue is emitted too). Use a plain `while (1)`; a goto loop does not produce it.

Best score 985 (target 28 insns, best attempt 25). Shape understood: s0=arg1; c=arg1[0] (ends up in a1 for the callback); p=arg1+1; load *p; if (*p & 0x80) p++ (gives arg1+2 fall-through / arg1+3 taken); then `lw v0,0(a0); addiu v1,zero,2; andi v0,v0,3; bne v0,v1`; if (arg0->unk0 & 3)==2 && D_802AC9D0 != NULL call D_802AC9D0(arg0->unk44, c); return p.
Blocker: KMC gcc if-converts `if (*p & 0x80) p++` into `p += (*p >> 7)` (srl+addu), while the ROM has a real branch (`lbu v0,0(s0); andi v0,0x80; beqz; addiu s0,s0,1 (delay, always); addiu s0,s0,1 (taken)`), i.e. 2 increments in the taken path and 1 in the fall-through (a plain `p++; if(bit) p++;` or `if (*p++ & 0x80) p++;` all if-convert). Tried: `if (*p++ & 0x80) p++;`, separate `p++; if (*p & 0x80) p++; p++;`, `p += 1; if (b & 0x80) p += 1;`, plus the struct/`Unk7548C` and callback forms. Nothing produced the two separate `addiu ...,1`s. Residual diffs also include reg flip of the `&3` compare (target: const 2 in v1, masked value in v0) and frame save order (target saves s0 before ra).
Next idea: find a C shape whose `if (bit)` body gcc 2.7.2 won't fold to an add (e.g. a statement gcc can't if-convert), or check whether the ROM part was built with different flags.

Best 235. Target (19 insns) is: p = func_80079A80(a0, a1) [call with NO argument setup: a0/a1 are simply forwarded, so the C must call it as func_80079A80(arg0, arg1) with those params]; then: move v1,v0 / move a0,v1 / lui v0,0xd00 / sw v0,0(a0) / load head=D_80111234 / addiu v1,v1,8 / lui v0,0x62e / sw v0,0(v1) / lw a0,0x48(head) / addiu v0,v1,8 / sw a0,4(v1) / jr. So the source has TWO base variables: q = p (kept in a0) and p = p + 2 words (v1), stores q[0]=0x0D000000, p[0]=0x062E0000, p[1]=D_80111234->unk48, return p + 2. Writing q[0],p[2],p[3] gives the right instructions but `sw 8(v1)`/`sw 0xc(v1)` instead of the materialized second base; `q=p; p+=2` (as done in func_80079A80, now at 98%) gives the exact shape. Remaining diff is REGISTER ALLOCATION only: target has q in a0, the 0x062E constant in v0, head in a0; my version put head in v0. Try reordering the p/q declarations or the head access to shift allocation. Data: D_80111234 is a game struct pointer; +0x48 is a u32 (probably a display-list pointer to append). func_80079A80 links two RDP-ish command words into the buffer arg1.

Jump-table dispatch, fully understood. Signature (UnkCE2C *arg0, s32 arg1, s32 arg2). switch (arg1) cases 1,4,9,7,8 (ROM block order = source case order) + default; idx = arg1-1, `sltiu idx,9`, `jr` through jtbl_801158E8 (0x801158E8, 9 entries, idx 1,2,4,5 -> default).
case1: arg0->unk00 = arg2; case4: unk20=0, unk24=1, unk30=0, unk1C=0 then if (arg0->unk00) arg0->unk00->unk8(obj,4,0); case9: unk30=1 then call (obj,9,0); case7: unk18=arg2; case8: unk1C=1; default: if (arg0->unk00) call (obj,arg1,arg2); all return 0.
BLOCKER (tooling, not C): a plain `switch` makes gcc put the table in .rodata and the judge says "your code refers to .rodata+0x0 where the ROM's code has no address" - unmatchable until the harness can map the compiler's switch table to jtbl_801158E8. Computed goto (`extern void *jtbl_801158E8[]; goto *jtbl_801158E8[idx];`) does reference the ROM symbol but gcc then deletes every case block as unreachable (no `&&label` address is taken; drops to 21 insns).
Best switch attempt: 1475. Residual beyond the table: target keeps arg0 in v1 too (`move v1,a0` in the beqz delay) and loads obj into a0 (`lw a0,0(a0)`), gcc used v1 for obj; target puts idx in a3, gcc in v1; target saves ra first.

BEST (310) source: u64 arg0; r=func_80086200(); u32 t=func_80087380(); u64 x=t; D_80325160=t; func_800873A0((s32)arg0+(s32)x,t); func_80086270(r);  -- this reproduces everything except (a) frame and (b) scheduling.

Semantics (settled): arg0 is a 64-bit value passed in a0/a1 (callers func_80081940 & func_80081A34 pass the u64 from func_80081BD0 / a 64-bit countdown; high=a0, low=a1). Only the LOW word is used. func_80087380 = mfc0 Count (u32), func_800873A0 = mtc0 Compare. D_80325160 is a u32 "last count" (u64 global D_80300720/724 exists separately). Target: t=Count; ONE dead `addu a0,zero,zero` (= high word of a ZERO-extended 32-bit value; sign-extension shows as sra and scores worse) before the store; store D_80325160=t; Compare = (s32)arg0low + t computed as `addu a0,s1,a1` IN THE jal delay slot (a1 holds t). A second arg a1=t is passed (func_800873A0 ignores it).

Remaining diff: 1) target frame 0x28 vs mine 0x20: outgoing=0x10, saved=0x10, so target has an 8-byte local slot that is NEVER accessed (no store/load to sp+0x10/0x14 anywhere). Something makes GCC reserve 8 bytes of locals while optimizing all accesses into registers (likely a 64-bit/aggregate local that is live enough to get a slot). 2) my builds compute `addu a0,<t>,s1` BEFORE the store and then redo `move a1,v0` in the delay slot; target keeps t in a1 and puts the sum in the slot. Tried: s32/u64/u32 locals, u64 now=return, (u32)arg0+x, various statement orders - none changed frame. Suggest a local aggregate/struct of 8 bytes used for the Count/compare (e.g. a two-word time struct) to force the slot; the sum should reference the same register a1 holds.

Target 27 insns, mine 29. TARGET uses NO callee-saved register: it recomputes &D_80300D98 (lui+addiu) before EACH of the three calls, saves only ra at 0x18 (frame 0x20). MINE keeps &D_80300D98 in s0 across the calls (extra save/restore s0 + one `move a0,s0`; frame 0x20 with ra at 0x1c). NOTE: func_8007A6E0 (the same init sequence without the third call) DOES use s0 and is matched - so the third call makes the difference. Not tried: making the third call's pointer a separate/different expression or local so gcc rematerializes the constant; maybe the 3rd call passes (void*)&D_80300D98 obtained via a different cast/macro. Cannot get closer by editing C: the 555 attempt already has all 45 instructions, operands and control flow identical — every remaining row is a register name, and I have exhausted the declaration/initialization orders (see the two distinct allocations below). Handing off the exact state.
DECODED BEHAVIOUR: arg1 = array of 4-byte records {s16 unk0; s8 unk2; s8 unk3;}, count D_803006C4; source blocks are D_802B0060[i] (8 bytes b0..b7). For each i: buf = block[i]; type = (buf.b2 & 0xC0) >> 4; rec[i].unk3 = type; if (type == 0) { rec[i].unk0 = buf.b4 | (buf.b5 << 8); bits |= 1 << i; rec[i].unk2 = buf.b6; } finally *arg0 = bits.
REQUIRED SOURCE SHAPE (score 555): declare `s32 bits = 0; u8 *flags = (u8 *)arg1 + 2; s16 *dst = (s16 *)arg1; SBlk8 *src = (SBlk8 *)D_802B0060; s32 i; SBlk8 buf; u8 type;` and in the loop body use flags[1]=type; if(type==0){*dst=...; bits|=1<<i; flags[0]=buf.b6;} then dst += 2; flags += 4;. The separate `flags` pointer is essential (otherwise gcc uses one base with displacements 2/3 and the operands are wrong). Loop `for (i = 0; i < D_803006C4; i++)`.
ALLOCATIONS SEEN: this shape gives src=t0 (matches), but flags=a3, dst=t2, i=a2, bits=t1. The initializer order (s32 bits=0; s32 i; SBlk8 buf; u8 type; SBlk8 *src=...; s16 *dst=...; u8 *flags=...) gives score 705 with dst=t0, src=t1, bits=t2, i=a2, flags=a3.
TARGET: arg0=t3, dst=t1 (copy of a1), bits=t2, src=t0, i=a3, flags=a2, the shift constant 1 in t4. Made no difference: swapping dst/src declarations, reordering the dst+=2/flags+=4 statements, writing the initialisations as statements in the emitted order (dst,bits,src,flags). Next idea: touch the type of one variable (e.g. declare bits as u32, or the loop var as s32 vs int) or split the initialisations across declarations, to perturb pseudo numbering.

Matched first try (47 insns). It initialises the 8-byte command block list: clears 15 words downwards from D_802B0098 (so D_802B0060..D_802B009B), sets D_802B009C = 1, builds the 8-byte block {0xFF,1,3,arg0,0xFF,0xFF,0xFF,0xFF}, copies it to &D_802B009C - 15 (=D_802B0060) D_803006C4 times advancing 8 bytes, then writes 0xFE after the last one. Things that mattered: `i = 14; p = (u32*)&D_802B0098; for (; i >= 0; i--) *p-- = 0;` (counter initialised BEFORE the pointer, else the two setup instructions swap); the copy destination must be an expression of D_802B009C (`dst = (u8 *)(end - 15);` with `end = &D_802B009C; *end = 1;`) so gcc emits `lui/addiu D_802B009C; addiu v1,-0x3C` rather than a direct D_802B0060 reference; the 8-byte copies must be a struct assignment (lwl/lwr + swl/swr).

Matched (8 insns). Doubly-linked list insert-after-sentinel: arg1 is a head/sentinel node, node->next at +0, node->prev at +4. C: `arg0->next = arg1->next; arg0->prev = arg1; if (arg1->next != NULL) arg1->next->prev = arg0; arg1->next = arg0;`. NOTE the statement order matters: writing `arg0->prev = arg1;` FIRST makes gcc emit the prev store before the `lw` of arg1->next and the diff stays at 60; the next-store must come first in the source (the peephole then puts the prev store between the load and the store). Do not cache arg1->next in a local: the ROM reloads it for the if (so it stays a second `lw`).

Matched (10 insns). Setter for a handler record: `s32 f(Rec *arg0, s32 arg1, s32 arg2) { switch (arg1) { case 1: arg0->unk00 = arg2; break; case 6: arg0->unk14 = arg2; break; } return 0; }`. It must be a SWITCH, not if/else-if: gcc then emits `beq a1,1,case1; beql a1,6,end` with the +0x14 store in the branch-likely delay slot, which is exactly the ROM (if/else-if gives `bnel` and stays at 580).

memcmp-like equality routine (u8 *p1, u8 *p2, s32 n) returning 0/1; called by func_80083D18/func_80084764 over 0x20-byte buffers. I believe it is hand-written assembly (SDK libc/memcmp), not C from this project's compiler. Evidence:
1) The same-alignment prefix compare is `addu $v0,$v1,$zero; lwl $v0,0($a0); lwl $v1,0($a1); bne`. The lone LWL pair compares exactly the (-p1&3) prefix bytes; the `addu v0,v1` seeds the untouched low bytes of both registers so they compare equal. That register-seeding trick is a hand optimization — no compiler emits it, and a plain `*(u32*)p1 != *(u32*)p2` cannot produce it.
2) Mixed `b` (one internal jump at .L80086804) and `j` (the two return-1 jumps) inside one function — an assembler author's choice; KMC gcc uses one form.
3) `slti $at,$a2,0x10`, `addiu $at,$zero,-4` allocate $at to C-level values (assembler-temporary style; gcc only uses $at for lui/constants).
4) Unaligned word compares: same-alignment path uses lw/lw, the different-alignment path uses lwl+lwr vs lw. A C compiler at -O2 (KMC gcc 2.7.2, the range's compiler) never emits lwl/lwr for a comparison — verified: the same semantics written as `*(u32*)p1 != *(u32*)p2` compiles to lw/lw.
Tried: plain byte-loop memcmp (score 6115, 14 insns vs 68), and the full word-at-a-time C reconstruction of the exact control flow (if n>=16; if ((p1^p2)&3)==0 { align prefix; 4-byte loop } else { align by p2; byte loop; unaligned-word loop }; byte tail) — KMC never emits lwl and the whole shape differs. IDO 7.1 would be the likely original toolchain (this 0x80085xxx-0x80086xxx SDK-libc region shows IDO-style $at/t-reg code, cf. notes on func_80086014/func_80085E1C) but ido-7.1 times out (>20s) in this project, so it cannot be tested. 3) The 64-byte table copy is a STRUCT assignment, and the whole local must be addressable so `n` stays in memory:
     typedef struct { u32 w[16]; } STbl;            /* 64 bytes, 4-byte members => lw/sw copy loop */
     typedef struct { STbl tbl; s32 n; } SLocal;    /* n at +0x40 */
     extern STbl D_80115850;
     SLocal s;
     ... s.tbl = D_80115850;                        /* gcc emits the 4-word/iter copy loop with a2/a3/t0 */
   The lookup `((f64 *)&s.tbl)[(s32)(x * D_801158B8) - 8]` takes the address of tbl, so gcc keeps `s.n` in memory (ROM's `lw/sw 0x40(sp)` inside both normalization loops + `lwc1 0x40(sp); cvt.d.w` in the base expression). A plain s32 n gets register-allocated and the frame shrinks to 0x40 (score 4114).
4) `base = (((table + n) * D_801158C0) / D_801158C8) + D_801158D0` (ln2, 2^30, 1.0). Normalization: first sign `v = x; if (!(x > 0.0)) v = -x;` (the delay-slot mov.d + neg.d on x); loops `while (D_801158A0 <= v) { v *= D_801158A8; n++; }` (1.0, 0.5) and `while (v < D_801158B0) { v = v + v; n--; }` (0.5; v+v gives the ROM's add.d, `v *= 2.0` puts a 2.0 in .rodata). Second sign needs a SEPARATE temp: `w = v; if (!(x > 0.0)) w = -w; x = w;` (in-place `v = -v` makes gcc negate v itself and drop the mov.d).
5) Exponent: `res = D_801158D0; while (e != 0) { if (e & 1) res *= base; e >>= 1; base *= base; }` then three `res = res * res;`.
6) Tail: `r = (s32)res; frac = (res - (f64)(f32)(s16)r) * D_801158D8; *arg5 = (s32)frac; return (s16)r;` — the (f32) step is required (cvt.s.w + cvt.d.s), and the store cast MUST be `(s32)`/plain, NOT `(u32)`: a (u32) cast makes gcc emit the 2^31-bias double->unsigned branch sequence (and a .rodata 2^31 constant, "refers to .rodata" warning). Matched on the 4th compile (270 insns). Three -O0 lessons this function needed:

1) MIN clamp: gcc-2.7.2's fold turns `a < b ? a : b` into MIN_EXPR(op0, op1); expand_expr's expand_operands evaluates op1 FIRST. So to reproduce a clamp whose ROM computes the cap A first and the sum B second (`A -> v1; B -> a0; slt v1,a0; if(A<B) a0=A; sw a0`), write the ternary the other way round: `D[i] = (B < A) ? B : A;` (B = D[i]+step first in source, A = cap). Writing `(A < B) ? A : B` gives the same semantics but B computed first (stack/reg diff). Same for the `&&` operands: `-D[i] < sp28 && sp28 > sp24` matched, `sp24 < sp28` loads sp24 first and does not.

2) The two 0x64-byte buffers must be 8-byte aligned with size rounded to 0x68 (`typedef union { u8 pad[0x64]; f64 align; } SBuf;`) to land at fp+0x30 and fp+0x98 after the s32 locals at 0x20/0x24/0x28. Scalars must be declared BEFORE the buffers (declaration order = ascending slots).

3) Buffer address args need a type conversion to get gcc's temp+copy (`addiu v0,fp,0x30; addu a3,v0,zero`) instead of a direct `addiu a3,fp,0x30`: declare the callees' buffer params as `void *` (e.g. `s32 func_80065E60(S63454Rec *, s32, s32, void *);`), not prototypeless.

Also: arg0 struct = {u8[0x460]; s32 flags[4][5] (stride 0x14, `lw 0x460(reg)` folds); u8[4]; s8 unk4B4;}. The three clamps multiply D_8009675C by 0x3E8 cap / 0x4B,0x32,0x19 step (1000/75/50/25) and the third uses cap 0x1F4 (500).

SOLVED THE BLOCK — same trick works here. func_8003F9F4 (the sibling right after this, same pattern) is now byte-identical. Two GCC 2.7.2 fold escape hatches combined:

1) Block the constant-migration fold `(A+K)+B -> A+(K+B)` by writing the constant as a STATEMENT EXPRESSION: `(arg4 + ({ 5; })) + ...`. TREE_CONSTANT of a STMT_EXPR is false, so fold can't move the constant; at expand time `({5;})` is just const 5, so it still compiles to `lw v1,arg4; addiu v0,v1,5` and the outer `+` then gets `addu v0,v0,s0` (target propagates into v0). NO extra instructions.
2) Block `A + -B -> A - B` (which otherwise emits subu and loses the `move v1,s0; negu a0,v1` sequence) by writing the negation as `({ x * -1; })`. KMC 2.7.2 does NOT fold `x * -1` to NEGATE, so it stays a MULT and expands to exactly `addu v1,s0,zero; negu a0,v1`. A plain `-x` (or `({-x;})`) gives `negu v1,s0` with no copy; `({x*-1;})` is required for the ROM's copy-then-neg.

ROM = gcc muldi3 expansion for the OPPOSITE DImode word order: with x=(a0=hi,a1=lo), y=(a2=hi,a3=lo) it computes hi(a0*a2) + lo(a1*a2) + lo(a0*a3) — the little-endian formula. MATCHED byte-exact (45/45) — new trick: load order of two adjacent byte reads. Target ROM order is `lbu v0,5(sp)` (b5) THEN `lbu v1,4(sp)` (b4); with plain C (`b5 = buf.b5; b4 = buf.b4; o->unk0 = b4 | (b5 << 8);`) GCC canonicalises the OR and emits the b4 load first (score 20, only the two loads swapped). Fix: force the b5 load at its statement position with `b5 = *(volatile u8 *)&buf[0].b5;` while b4 stays a normal read, then `o->unk0 = b4 | (b5 << 8);`. The volatile cast keeps the load instruction/order identical (no extra insns) and the OR stays `or v1,v1,v0`. Also load-bearing: `n = D_803006C4;` re-read AFTER `s++` and BEFORE `o++` inside the do-while (that puts the count `lbu` between s++ and the o++ `addiu a2`), and b6 read into a temp BEFORE `bits |= 1 << i` (keeps `lbu v1,6(sp)` before the sllv).

MATCHED (score 0, 53/53) after ~110 attempts by 5 agents. The wall was the two indirect call sites: ROM is `move a0,$v1; lw $v0,8($a0)` (fn pointer loaded through the OUTGOING-ARG register, after the arg copy), ours kept emitting `lw $v0,8($v1); move a0,$v1`.

Working idiom (pure C, no asm):
1. load the child into a local BEFORE the field stores so the test keeps it in $v1: `c = arg0->unk0;` then the stores, then `if (c != NULL)`;
2. inside the if, copy it into a SECOND local and call through THAT local for both the base and the argument: `d = c; d->unk8(d, 4);`.
Then the allocator gives arg0=$a0, c=$v1, d=$a0 (outgoing-arg preference), so it emits exactly `move $a0,$v1; lw $v0,8($a0)`.
Key facts learned: (a) `arg0->unk0->unk8(arg0->unk0, N)` (one expression) gives right colours but `lw v0,8(v1); move a0,v1` (score 400); (b) re-reading `arg0->unk0` after the stores is NOT CSE'd (the stores invalidate it) and emits an extra `lw a0,($a0)` (470) — so the copy must come from the held local, not memory; (c) the default case must stay the plain direct expression `arg0->unk0->unk8(arg0->unk0, arg1)` (there the child goes straight into $a0); (d) case 3 needs the alias `p = (SChild*)arg0` used only for the final `p->unk40 = arg2` store, which is what puts `addu $v1,$a0,$zero` in the first beq delay slot.

MATCHED (201/201) with the MIN/MAX macro idiom, not the register-variable clamp. Key finding: writing a clamp as macros

#define MIN6(a,b) ((a) < (b) ? (a) : (b))
#define MAX6(a,b) ((a) >= (b) ? (a) : (b))

D_8029DFA0 = MIN6(MAX6(D_8029DFA0 + D_8029DFA8, 0), D_80097EEC[D_80097EE4]);

makes GCC 2.7.2 fold the ?: into MIN_EXPR/MAX_EXPR: the table read is evaluated ONCE (no duplicated lh/loads) and its operand stays a compiler temporary, so local-alloc uses $v0 for the address temp AND the loaded value (target: lw v0 / move v1,v0 / sll v0,v1 / lui a0 / addu v1,v0,a0 / lh v0), with the clamp result in $v1. All previous 88 attempts used `register s32 limit` which pins $v0 for the whole block and gives 40. The MACRO ARGUMENT ORDER decides evaluation order: MIN6(table, max) evaluates max first (score 3020); MIN6(max, table) evaluates table first = the ROM (score 0). So if a folded MIN/MAX comes out with the arguments evaluated in the wrong order, SWAP the macro arguments. The `>=` in MAX6 gives the ROM's bgez; plain `>` would give bgtz. MAX6(a,0) then `move $v0,$zero` vs ROM `addu $v1,zero,zero` also falls out correctly once order and register pressure are right.

1) D_803246FB is not a separate table: it is D_803246E0+0x1B (the +0x1B byte of the 0x1C-stride record). The target store is a POST-DECREMENT, so declare `extern u8 D_803246E0[][0x1C];` and write `D_803246E0[sp14][0x1B]--;`. That single form produces the dead index prelude (a0), the materialised `%hi(D_803246E0)+%lo` base, `lbu/addiu -1/move a0,v1/sb 0x1B(v0)` — the exact block (same idiom as func_8004E4A8's `u16 E0[][10]; E0[i][0x235]++;`). The condition/call-arg reads stay signed: `extern s8 D_803246FB[][0x1C]; D_803246FB[i][0]` (lb), and `extern s8 D_803246FA[][0x1C]; D_803246FA[i][0]=-1` (sb).
2) The `%s %s` call is NOT the else of `if (!(...))` — it is the statement AFTER that if-block: `if (!(cond)) { if (FB&&FA) {...return 0;} else {...return 5;} } func_80080110(BB0,B28,...);` This moves the dead inner-if join jump to the right place and fixes all branch displacements.
3) Case 0x14's `if (D_80097781 == 0) return 0;` is really `if (D_80097781 != 0) { ...return 8; } break;` — the outer if's skip block ends in the case break, which is the ROM's end stub `j return0; nop` (beqz to it), instead of an inlined bnez+j+move.

1) The routine implements u64/u32 division where (a0,a1)=hi:lo dividend, a3=divisor, returns the quotient in v0:v1 (high:low) and DELIBERATELY leaves the 32-bit remainder in $t1 (the `mfhi $t1` near the end is never read inside this function). See notes on func_80089D40/80089D60 (already set aside).
3) Also leaves the final remainder in a0:a1 by modifying the argument regs in place - again a register convention, not a return value.

Best C attempts (3 compiles, best score 3190/50 insns): reconstructed the exact algorithm (normalise the 32-bit high remainder, quotient estimate v/(d>>k + 1), 64-bit multiply back and subtract) with u32 hi/lo/divisor params + u64 quotient; it matches the arithmetic/chunk order but cannot reproduce the t1 remainder side effect or the DImode product/sub shape; extra shifts appear whenever a u64 word is extracted, and the dead mfhi t1 is unreachable. 4 u32 params (hi,lo,dhi,dv) compiles cleanest (no u64 param extraction junk) but still 16+ extra/regalloc rows.
